rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a nanoscale Al2O3 interlayer between Cr and Zr-alloy, while the paper uses compositionally varied AlTiCrZrNbTa coatings with different Al contents. These are fundamentally different interventions (a diffusion barrier interlayer vs. a compositionally modified coating), so the hypothesis does not reconstruct the paper's intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions subcritical water (300–400°C) and high-temperature steam (900–1000°C), while the paper tests isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C. Both involve high-temperature steam, but the hypothesis includes a subcritical water regime not tested in the paper and lacks the paper's specific steam flow rate and cooling method.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a physical diffusion barrier (Al2O3 interlayer) to prevent Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on the formation of a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion. These are different classes of mechanisms (diffusion barrier vs. protective oxide formation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and improved adhesion/performance relative to an unmodified Cr coating, while the paper predicts and measures a minimum oxidation rate and oxygen penetration at an intermediate Al content. The properties and directions differ (interdiffusion vs. oxidation resistance), and the paper's outcome is not predicted.
